Subject: DPA — archival TTL and backup carve-outs (follow-up)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call earlier this week. Our legal team reviewed the DPA redlines and flagged two related areas where we need clearer language before we can proceed: archival/long-term retention and backup copies. Specifically: 

- We need a firm definition of "archival TTL" (how long Redwood will retain archived snapshots tied to customer data) and whether archives are subject to the same deletion trigger as primary storage.
- Backup copies: the draft allows for "short-term backups" but doesn't specify maximum retention, nor whether backups that contain customer data will be stored outside the US for failover.
- Exceptions: we expect carve-outs for legal hold and for machine-learning model training provenance. We want to see explicit language limiting use for training without opt-in.

Attached is our suggested redline (Acme_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx) with example language. Can you confirm Redwood's standard position on archive TTL and whether you can accept a 90-day max backup retention for backups that include PII, with an onshore-only storage requirement?

If it helps, we'd like a short written response we can take to our SOC/compliance board.

Best,
Maya Patel
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the redlines and for calling this out. I've reviewed your attachment and summarized Redwood's standard positions below, plus one compromise we can offer for Acme Health. Short version: we can meet you on backup retention and onshore constraints with a scoped exception model. Longer details below.

Proposed Redwood positions (default):
- Archival TTL: Redwood retains customer archives for 18 months by default to support incident forensics and restore operations. Archives are considered subject to customer deletion requests and the DPA erasure flow, except when retained for lawful hold.
- Backups: standard backup TTL is 90 days for operational backups; however, snapshots retained for disaster recovery (DR) may be kept longer (up to 12 months) for certain customers with dedicated capacity. Backups may be replicated across regions for failover unless the customer requests a geofence.
- Training use: Redwood does not use customer-provided data to train models unless there is an explicit opt-in and a separate agreement. Telemetry used for quality is aggregated and de-identified.

Acme-specific compromise (we can accept):
- Agreed archival TTL for Acme Health: 12 months (rather than our 18-month default) for archival snapshots that are tagged as "Acme-production".
- Backups: We will cap backups containing PII at 90 days and commit to storing those backup copies onshore (US only) when Acme requests this in writing.
- DR snapshots: If DR snapshots are required across regions, we'll provide a formal exception workflow that requires written approval and logging/audit of cross-border access.

Next steps:
1) If this direction works for Acme, we'll prepare a short DPA appendix with the language change for archival TTL and backup constraints.
2) We will run the appendix past our security team and provide a one-page compliance statement you can share with your SOC board.

Looping in Laura and Rishi for any risk/ops/implementation notes below.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Laura —

Quick operational notes (summary of Slack discussion with Storage and DR teams):

- Account-level archival TTL tag: feasible. We'll implement a metadata flag "ttl_override: 12m" for Acme-production. This will cause archival snapshots to be pruned at 12 months by the existing lifecycle job. Estimated engineering lead time: 2 business days to schedule and 5 business days to roll (no downtime).
- Onshore-only backup routing: two options:
  1) Tag-and-route: tag backups that contain PII and route to US-only buckets within the same backup pipeline. No dedicated pool required; needs config change + an automated verification job. Dev effort: ~3 business days.
  2) Dedicated pool: heavier option, 2-3 weeks, adds cost.
- Auditability: We can emit an immutable event to the compliance audit log on any cross-region DR snapshot copy/access. The events will include operator, timestamp, justification, and DocuSign reference if required. Implementation ETA: 3 business days for logging hooks + 1 day to generate the 1-page compliance statement.

Recommendation: implement tag-and-route (option 1) and add the immutable audit hook. That meets the 90-day backup cap and onshore requirement with minimal customer friction.

I'll draft the operations paragraph for the appendix and the compliance statement after Kimberly signs off.

—Rishi

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the redlines and patience while we scoped internally. Based on ops feedback, Redwood can accept the following language for the DPA appendix specific to Acme Health: 

1) Archival TTL: Redwood will retain archival snapshots tagged as "Acme-production" for a maximum of 12 months from snapshot creation. These archives will be subject to customer-initiated deletion requests and the DPA erasure flow, except where retention is required by lawful hold.

2) Backups with PII: Redwood will cap retention for backups containing customer PII at 90 days. At Acme Health's written request, Redwood will store backups that contain PII in US-only storage locations. Storage and retrieval will follow Redwood's documented access controls and encryption standards.

3) DR snapshot exceptions: Cross-region DR replication that includes Acme data will require a documented exception (written approval from Acme), creation of an audit record (immutable log entry with operator, timestamp, and justification), and will be time-bound per the exception request.

4) Training prohibition: Redwood confirms it will not use Acme's customer-provided data to train models without explicit opt-in. Aggregated/anonymous telemetry used for quality improvements will not contain PII.

We've attached a short appendix draft (RWI_Archival_TTL_Proposal_20290513.pdf) and we'll provide a one-page compliance statement you can use with your SOC board. If this is acceptable, please confirm and we'll convert the appendix into tracked changes for your redline doc and prepare the DocuSign.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference
